cohort: The study included all singleton live births to adolescent and young adult women (ages 15-39 years) diagnosed with cancer during pregnancy in Texas from January 1999 to December 2016 (n=1291), compared to a 1:4 matched control group of women without cancer (n=5084).
finding: Adolescent and young adult women diagnosed with cancer during pregnancy had a significantly higher prevalence of adverse birth outcomes, including low birth weight, very preterm birth, preterm birth, cesarean delivery, low Apgar score, and heart and circulatory system defects, compared to women without cancer.
mod_finding: AYA women diagnosed with cancer during pregnancy had a higher prevalence of cesarean delivery (44.3%) compared to women without cancer (35.2%).
birth_weight: N/A (low birth weight was an outcome, not an inclusion criterion for all babies)
